topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
usual_baseline: Virtual fracture clinics generally meet the 72-hour review: mean 2.33 days [1249], 93.8% within 72 hours [1330]. Without one, 6% were seen in time [1538]. Referral quality is the weak point: 21% suitable for direct ED discharge [1222], 32.1% of ED upper limb referrals had errors [1777]. Advanced imaging waits reach 30 days.
fix_that_works: Introducing a VFC: 6% to 100% within 72 hours [1538]. Mandatory VFC triage and early discharge cut face-to-face appointments by 50.2% [1694]. Joint ED guidelines: inappropriate referrals 80 to 24 [1327], errors 32.1% to 12.6% [1777]. ED education: soft tissue referrals 15.1% to 4.5% [1367]. Radiology priority slots: imaging wait 4.51 to 3.56 days [1316].
fix_that_fails: Clinic logistics barely changed: appointment wait 3.55 to 3.21 days, waiting area still rated inadequate by 41.49% [1550]. Radial head fractures were still seen in clinic in 64% [1367]. Virtual discharge fell from 17.9% to 13.6% [1611].
consultant_advice: The 72-hour standard is usually met once a VFC exists, so auditing it again adds little. More useful: the quality of ED referrals, delays to advanced imaging, and patient safety or satisfaction after virtual discharge, which one large audit said was not assessed [1694].
